findings: Both r3 findings are fixed. (a) The S2 off-by-one and race in M1 (lines 91-94) is gone. The single shared counter is now two private counters, drv_cycle and mon_cycle, each incremented as the first statement after its own clocking-block event. Each item is stamped accept = c + 1. I checked this against IEEE 1800-2023: 14.16 says a zero-skew drive with no cycle delay is scheduled in the Re-NBA region of the current time step, and 14.10 says the clocking block event fires in the Observed region, so the drive comes after the DUT flops have sampled at edge c. 14.13 says #1step samples the value from just before the edge, so mon_cb first sees the input at c + 1. 14.3 makes #0 the default output skew. The stamp therefore equals mon_cycle on the clean DUT. The monitor's three steps (check outputs, then inputs, then reset) also hold up for a reset arriving one or two edges after an input is accepted. (b) The S3 on Mutant 1 (line 102) now says both stages are clocked on the falling edge. I traced it: accepted at k = c + 1, stage 2 captures at the falling edge before c + 2, so mon_cb sees out_valid at k + 1 and the latency check catches it. Mutant 3 (line 104) is caught however the race resolves, because mon_cb sees the late drive at c + 2, one edge after its stamp.

The other changed statements are correct. M0 line 52: a process woken by @(posedge clk) reads q before the DUT's nonblocking update, because the NBA region runs after the Active region (IEEE 1800-2023, 4.4.2.2 and 4.4.2.4); checking on the falling edge works. M2 line 141: the 4-entry FIFO (line 132) supports 'up to four items'. M5 lines 252/258: a KEY write takes effect at the rising edge after its access phase completes, and the sequence never lets an input transfer and a KEY write complete at the same edge, so the two monitors' write() order within one time step cannot decide a prediction. M7 line 342: writing a non-reset value before mirror(UVM_CHECK) is correct, since mirror with UVM_CHECK compares the read-back value with the mirrored value (IEEE 1800.2-2020, 18.4.4.14; I took this from memory and did not search uvm_lrm.txt for it).

Resolved: r3 S2 (intended-cycle off-by-one and shared counter race). Now projects-data.ts:93 gives each process its own counter, each one incremented as the first statement after its own clocking event, so there is no shared state. Line 94 stamps c + 1. I checked the reasoning against IEEE 1800-2023 14.16: zero-skew clocking outputs 'schedule new values in the Re-NBA region of the time step corresponding to the clocking event', which is after the DUT flops sample at edge c, so mon_cb with #1step sees the input at c + 1. The cited clauses 14.10, 14.13, 14.16 and 4.7 exist with those titles. The monitor's step order (outputs, then inputs, then reset) is correct. Reset at edge k deletes only the items still in flight. The sent queue is written at edge c and read at c + 1 at the earliest, and the expected-output queue has a single owner, so the claim that results do not depend on process order holds.

Resolved: r3 S3 (Mutant 1). Line 102 now says both stages clock on the falling edge, and the trace holds: driven at c, accepted by the monitor at k = c + 1, out_valid seen at c + 2 = k + 1, so step 1 pops an item that is not yet due. Mutant 2 (out_valid not 1 at the due edge) and Mutant 3 (mon_cb sees the input one edge after its stamp) are both caught by the checks as written.

Other changes in the diff are clear, correct and achievable. M0 drives on the falling edge and checks there, which removes the posedge read-before-NBA trap. M2 waits for N output transfers plus a timeout before dropping the objection, which matches the 4-entry FIFO. M5 defines when a KEY write takes effect relative to an accepted byte and explains why write() order within one time step never decides a prediction. M7 writes a value other than the reset value before mirror(UVM_CHECK). M1's interface initial values make rst_n and in_valid variables, which is consistent with the clocking-drive rules.
